summary.en: Spanish expresses liking and minding backwards: the thing liked drives the verb, while me, te or le marks the person.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 3.

Stepping into the quiet attic room, Javier beams *¡Me encanta este espacio!*, and Mateo checks *¿No le importa subir más escaleras?* Later Carmen recalls two boys from the street: *al pequeño le encantaban los trenes*. Verbs of liking and reaction—*gustar* ('to please / be liked'), *encantar* ('to delight / love'), and *importar* ('to matter / mind')—flip the English sentence structure.

Instead of 'I love this space', Spanish says 'this space delights me': an indirect pronoun (*me*, *te*, *le*, *nos*, *les*) marks who feels the reaction, while the verb agrees with what triggers it. Use the singular form before one noun or an infinitive (*me gusta el patio*, *me encanta este espacio*, *¿no le importa subir?*), and the plural -n form before plural nouns (*me gustan las llaves*, *le encantaban los trenes*).

Because *le* can mean 'to him', 'to her', or 'to you' (*usted*), Spanish often adds *a* + person in front (*al pequeño le encantaban*) whenever context needs clarifying.
